aesthetic: The Spark and the Receipt — a big-box ad console closing the loop
anchor: Walmart's own retail identity — the deep-blue fascia and the six-petal yellow Spark of 'Save Money. Live Better.' — crossed with the two instruments this deal is actually about: the thermal POS receipt (the closed-loop proof that a TV ad drove a measured store sale) and the self-serve media-buying console Vibe sells (the '$50/day, launch a TV ad in minutes' dashboard). The world is a retail-media operations screen: navy ground, a single spark-gold accent, conversion-green and spend-red metrics, a CTV-screen cyan, and receipt-mono numbers.
rationale: The corpus's structural metaphor is a CLOSED LOOP and a COMPLETED STACK — Walmart spent two years assembling data (Connect), screen (VIZIO), and pipes, and bought Vibe to snap in the missing self-serve front door, closing a loop from impression to purchase. So the figures should read like a market dashboard and a receipt, not a humanities study: grotesque deck-headline display, a sans brief body, and true monospace for the deal's many numbers. The accent is WALMART SPARK GOLD, deliberately set apart from the cool greens/teals/cobalt and the magentas of the other ad-tech corpora on the shelf, and pushed brighter/purer than the two amber corpora (india-advertising, uap) so it separates in both light and dark. The figure palette pairs the gold (the Spark / Vibe / the deal) with a Walmart true-blue (data and demand), a conversion-green (the measured sale / ROAS), a spend-red (cost and leakage), a CTV-screen cyan (the streaming surface), and a receipt-graphite. Warm receipt-paper for day; a deep retail-navy 'ops screen at night' for dark.

fonts.display: 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, 'Segoe UI', Arial, system-ui, sans-serif
